shape/literal.go.patch:
--- a/shape/literal.go
+++ b/shape/literal.go
@@ -31,6 +31,7 @@
 - status: required, superseded, informal or secret;
 - package_value: the value that the package uses in its place, empty when there is none;
 - why: one short reason.
+Every item carries every field, including status: all six fields literal, source, source_quote, status, package_value and why are present on every item, and a field with nothing to say is the empty string, never omitted.
 A required literal is a value that the request or a settled answer explicitly requires the implementation or an example to use exactly, such as a path, command, name, identifier, number or example input; descriptive text that may be paraphrased is not a literal.
 Give status superseded for a value that the request or a later answer explicitly replaces, and status secret for secret material such as a password, token, key or credential; for secret material leave literal, source_quote, package_value and why empty.
 Copy each literal exactly as its source writes it, with source_quote copied exactly from that source and containing the literal; Kogen itself compares each literal with the package byte for byte.
@@ -52,8 +53,8 @@
 			"source":        s,
 			"source_quote":  s,
 			"package_value": s,
-			"why":           s,
-			"status":        map[string]any{"type": "string", "enum": []any{"required", "superseded", "informal", "secret"}},
+			"why":           map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "Present on every item, never omitted: one short reason, or the empty string when there is nothing to say (always for a secret item)."},
+			"status":        map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "Present on every item, never omitted: exactly one of required, superseded, informal or secret; a secret item still carries status secret.", "enum": []any{"required", "superseded", "informal", "secret"}},
 		},
 		"required":             []any{"literal", "source", "source_quote", "package_value", "why", "status"},
 		"additionalProperties": false,

shape/decision.go.patch:
--- a/shape/decision.go
+++ b/shape/decision.go
@@ -26,6 +26,7 @@
 - verdict: follows (the request, a recorded answer, or an evidenced or assumed Decision supports the value), contradicts (the request states a different value), consequence (no quote states it, but it follows from quoted request text and contradicts nothing in the request) or unsupported (none supports it);
 - intent_value, request_value and difference: the two values and what makes them differ, for contradicts only;
 - why: one short reason.
+Every item carries every field, including why: all seven fields statement, request_quotes, verdict, intent_value, request_value, difference and why are present on every item, and a field with nothing to say is the empty string (an empty list for request_quotes), never omitted.
 Give consequence, with the request quote it follows from, for a statement that is a plausible consequence of request text (what the request implies, such as a refusal status or a label for something the request asks for), a testable restatement of a request instruction (a marker, example or measurement that checks what the request asks), or a detail the request leaves to the builder and does not decide otherwise. Never give consequence when the statement differs from any value the request gives, narrows, removes or adds scope the request does not ask for, or has no request passage to quote; give contradicts or unsupported then.
 Compare values, not notation: before comparing, normalise digit grouping (1,000 and 1000), percentages and fractions (50% and 0.5), units of the same quantity (2 minutes and 120 seconds), date layouts, the order of a list whose order does not matter, and letter case where case does not matter.
 A statement that restates the request's value in another notation follows the request.
@@ -51,7 +52,7 @@
 			"intent_value":   s,
 			"request_value":  s,
 			"difference":     s,
-			"why":            s,
+			"why":            map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "Present on every item, never omitted: one short reason, or the empty string when there is nothing to say."},
 		},
 		"required":             []any{"statement", "request_quotes", "verdict", "intent_value", "request_value", "difference", "why"},
 		"additionalProperties": false,

shape/literal.go.patch:
--- a/shape/literal.go
+++ b/shape/literal.go
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@
 - why: one short reason.
 Every item carries every field, including status: all six fields literal, source, source_quote, status, package_value and why are present on every item, and a field with nothing to say is the empty string, never omitted.
 A required literal is a value that the request or a settled answer explicitly requires the implementation or an example to use exactly, such as a path, command, name, identifier, number or example input; descriptive text that may be paraphrased is not a literal.
-Give status superseded for a value that the request or a later answer explicitly replaces, and status secret for secret material such as a password, token, key or credential; for secret material leave literal, source_quote, package_value and why empty.
+Give status superseded for a value that the request or a later answer explicitly replaces, and status secret for secret material such as a password, token, key or credential.
 Copy each literal exactly as its source writes it, with source_quote copied exactly from that source and containing the literal; Kogen itself compares each literal with the package byte for byte.
 Give status informal for a value that appears only in informal background, an aside or an example the source marks optional; Kogen never demands an informal value.
 This check covers the requested product behavior and examples, not the procedure used to shape the Intent. A command, tool name, parameter or artifact handle mentioned only in instructions to the shaper (inspect, probe, generate, retain or submit) is not a product literal: give it status informal. Those process instructions can still be mandatory for Shape to execute; they do not require the Intent to describe or prove Shape's tool calls. If the requested product itself exposes that same name or value, it remains required. For example, "use a probe with capture_output=true and propose_files from_probe to prepare the proof" imposes no such product literals, while "add a probe parameter named capture_output" requires capture_output in the product contract.
